# Xintong Han

> Xintong Han is an Assistant Professor of Marketing in the Department of Marketing at the Faculty of Business Administration, Université Laval.

Canonical profile: https://han-xintong.github.io/
Academic background: https://han-xintong.github.io/about/
Official university profile: https://www.fsa.ulaval.ca/en/expert/xintong-han/
ORCID: https://orcid.org/0000-0001-7369-0506
Google Scholar: https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=ZbgMprUAAAAJ&hl=en
Email: xintong.han@fsa.ulaval.ca

## Research

Xintong Han studies digital platforms, pricing policies, and networks, using structural econometrics, causal inference, and machine learning in econometrics.

## Selected peer-reviewed publications

- [Digital revitalization or useless effort? Public e-commerce support and local specialty sales](https://han-xintong.github.io/research/public-ecommerce-support/) (2026)
  - Authors: Xintong Han, Jan Victor Dee, Shaojia Wang & Kefan Chen
  - Publication: Journal of Development Economics, 179, 103665. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jdeveco.2025.103665
  - Setting and method: Pu’er tea farmers in China · Staggered platform rollout and household panel data
  - Finding: Platform access increased online sales by 16.649% and decreased offline sales by 15.549%, while total sales remained broadly unchanged.
  - Interpretation: The intervention combines platform access with complementary support. Estimates use the staggered rollout and household panel data; they should not be interpreted as the effect of a randomly assigned, stand-alone online storefront.
  - Citation: https://han-xintong.github.io/research/public-ecommerce-support/citation.bib
- [Effectiveness of online education during the COVID-19 pandemic: Evidence from Chinese universities](https://han-xintong.github.io/research/online-education/) (2026)
  - Authors: Xintong Han, Shijie Lu, Xin (Shane) Wang & Nan Cui
  - Publication: Production and Operations Management, 35(3), 978–994. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1177/10591478251361979
  - Setting and method: Nine Chinese universities · Pandemic-induced transition to online learning
  - Finding: Online education increased mathematics scores by 8–11 points on a 100-point scale; effects varied with course type and lockdown policies.
  - Interpretation: The evidence concerns the pandemic transition in the sampled universities and courses. Mathematics-score gains are measured in points, not percentages, and do not imply equal benefits across all subjects or online-learning settings.
  - Citation: https://han-xintong.github.io/research/online-education/citation.bib
- [Nonlinear pricing in multidimensional context: An empirical analysis of energy consumption](https://han-xintong.github.io/research/nonlinear-energy-pricing/) (2023)
  - Authors: Xintong Han, Zimin Liu & Tong Wang
  - Publication: International Journal of Industrial Organization, 91, 103034. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijindorg.2023.103034
  - Setting and method: Household electricity use in Hangzhou, China · Structural demand estimation
  - Finding: The structural estimates imply that a 1% price increase reduces total electricity demand by about 0.7%, with limited scope for further tariff optimization.
  - Interpretation: The elasticity and tariff counterfactuals are model-based implications of the observed pricing environment, rather than experimental estimates of a tariff reform.
  - Citation: https://han-xintong.github.io/research/nonlinear-energy-pricing/citation.bib
- [Peer recognition, badge policies, and content contribution: An empirical study](https://han-xintong.github.io/research/peer-recognition/) (2023)
  - Authors: Xintong Han, Yushen Li & Tong Wang
  - Publication: Journal of Economic Behavior & Organization, 214, 691–707. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jebo.2023.08.021
  - Setting and method: Zhihu contributors in China · Panel analysis with instrumental variables
  - Finding: Peer votes encourage content creation, while identity-rich badges can constrain contributions through reputation and privacy concerns.
  - Interpretation: Results concern peer voting and the particular badge policies studied on Zhihu. They do not establish that all forms of recognition or visibility increase participation.
  - Citation: https://han-xintong.github.io/research/peer-recognition/citation.bib

## Selected working papers

- Creator platform commission design. With Pu Zhao, Guanghua School of Management, Peking University, and Bin Gu, Questrom School of Business, Boston University.
  - Summary: Examines how a platform’s move from a uniform 5% commission to 20%, followed by selective reductions to 5%, changed creator prices and content quality.
- Technology adoption in input-output networks. With Lei Xu · NET Institute Working Paper #18-05 · Bank of Canada Staff Working Paper 2019-51
  - Summary: Models Python 3 adoption when a software package’s adoption cost depends on whether its dependency packages support Python 3.
  - Source: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3266251
  - Additional source: https://www.bankofcanada.ca/2019/12/staff-working-paper-2019-51/
